store.title: Lantern Row
store.subtitle: Merge snacks, fill each order
store.shortDescription: Merge street snacks at dusk and fill each paper order, one line at a time.
store.description:
Drag a snack onto its twin and the two become one finer snack. A Pepper Skewer turns into a Twin Skewer, then a Glazed Skewer, and eight steps up into a Dragon Grill Board. Each stall's gear drops a fresh snack onto the board below the street every 4 seconds.

Customers step up to the counters holding paper tickets: a fox, a hedgehog, a badger, an otter. Each ticket asks for one to three snacks, and you drag each snack onto its line. A ticket pays its printed price only once every line is filled; then it is stamped and folds into a paper lantern. Who is waiting decides what you merge next.

Coins open new stalls and more of the board, and make each stall's gear finer: higher levels drop better snacks, never faster ones. Six stalls light up in turn: grill, tea, steamer, sweets, noodles, and puffs from the second season.

Each season ends with a Festival ticket on the street banner. Fill it, and close the season when you choose: coins, stalls and levels start again, while board space, lanterns, the Ladder Book and seasoned gear stay. Seasons change the street: a moon gate one season, braziers in the corners another, fireflies over the stalls.

Twenty lanterns hang on the Lantern Gate, each lit once by something you did. The Ladder Book keeps every snack you have made. Now and then a paper dragon comes down the street with a gold ticket that pays double.

The idle part, in full: minders you hire put a house snack's price in the till every 15 seconds, while you play and while the app is closed, for up to 4 hours at a time; in those hours away your gear fills its shelf with up to 6 snacks. Some lanterns and seasons raise these numbers: one lantern adds 2 more hours away. Look in a few times a day and most of your coins will come from the till. What the till cannot do is merge, fill a ticket, light a lantern or close a season: every merge, and the last line of every ticket, is yours to place.

No energy. Orders never time out. Ads are optional, and gift box odds are shown before you open one. Gift boxes are earned by filling tickets; none are for sale.

Three optional purchases: Blue Silk Awnings for every stall (looks only), Late Hours for 4 more hours away, and Quiet Evening, which gives every ad reward without the video.

store.title: Orbit Haulers
store.subtitle: Space mining by drone routes
store.shortDescription: An asteroid field, a hold of ore, and a freighter waiting for your swipe.
store.description:
Orbit Haulers is an idle mining game about routes and cargo.

Your station sits in an asteroid field. Drag hauler drones onto rocks to set their routes, and watch them carry ore home to the hold. When the hold is full, swipe the freighter off the pad: it warps out and the whole manifest sells at once.

Buyers post contracts for the ores they want: so many units within a few launches. Take one, send drones to the rocks that carry its ore, and when the last units arrive the buyer pays its rate on all of them.

Rocks run dry and new ones drift in, sometimes with a different ore, sometimes as a rich bonanza rock. The far rings hold copper, ice, titanium and platinum, but the trips are longer, so where you send each drone matters.

Bring the dock autopilot online and the station ships on its own while you are away. Fit modules into three sockets in the Fitting Bay; some of them change the rules. When a run has paid off, jump to a new galaxy, spend Warp Cores on the Star Map, and choose the conditions you will mine under next.

Features
- Drag-to-route drones on a top-down map of the asteroid field
- One-swipe freighter launches and buyer contracts delivered over several launches
- Rocks that run dry and come back as new ore
- A dock autopilot that keeps shipping offline
- Fitting Bay modules and a Star Map that changes how each run starts
- Optional rewarded ads; salvage pods are earned in play, never sold
